plan.topic: Family comments at the Thanksgiving table about how little you're eating on tirzepatide: what the label says about appetite, and calm, guilt-free ways to handle the moment
plan.angle: On tirzepatide and someone says, 'That's all you're eating?' Relief fact, quoted from the Zepbound PI section 12.2: tirzepatide reduces food intake. Untagged tips, 2 at most: a friendly reply ready ahead of time (you don't owe anyone health details), and boxing a plate for later is fine. Mindset: weight is one health measure among many, and the people count as much as the plate. Add the disordered-eating line pointing to the care team, and the diabetes plus insulin or sulfonylurea low-blood-sugar line. Then the on-screen pancreatitis card in Medication Guide wording, the scoped don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber.' and the loop line. No calorie, 'bad food' or eat-less-as-a-goal messaging.

Fixes: (1) The 'label wording' has to be the Zepbound or Mounjaro PI's actual sentence from section 12.2 (e.g. that tirzepatide lowers body weight and reduces food intake, with GLP-1 described as a regulator of appetite). Open the PI and quote it exactly, or paraphrase it without claiming it's the label's words. (2) The disordered-eating line should point to support without any eating instruction: 'If you've had disordered eating, follow your care team's plan.' That's fine. Don't add anything suggesting eating less is the goal. (3) Add the eating-less safety sign on screen. Use the full Medication Guide pancreatitis wording, 'severe pain in your stomach area that won't go away, with or without vomiting … right away', and the scoped don't-stop line. (4) Keep the low-blood-sugar line scoped to diabetes plus insulin or a sulfonylurea, without implying zero risk otherwise. (5) Confirm the Thanksgiving long video is actually live before using it as the related-video target. If it isn't, use Side Effects.

package.title: Tirzepatide at Thanksgiving: "That's All You're Eating?" #shorts
package.description:
Thanksgiving table comments hit different on tirzepatide. Here's a calm, guilt-free way to answer, and what the label says about appetite.

With type 2 diabetes, insulin or a sulfonylurea alongside it may raise low blood sugar risk. It's reported without type 2 diabetes too. Call your healthcare provider right away if you have severe pain in your stomach area that won't go away, with or without vomiting. For anything that isn't that emergency sign, don't stop or change your medicine on your own. #Tirzepatide

Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

script.cta:
Spoken ending: "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber. You're ready for the next time you're…" This loops back into sentence 1. There is no subscribe line and no "link in the description".

Post notes (Exp G): the related-video target is the Thanksgiving on Tirzepatide long video. Its row in the 11-21 snapshot (140 lifetime minutes) hasn't changed in 3 days, so the owner should confirm it is live before linking it. If it isn't live, use Side Effects.

Word count: 160 (standard arm, 135–160). The fact-checker's s6 line is 23 spoken words, not the 21 it estimated, so two more words came out of non-safety lines:
- s3: "your health details" became "health details", which matches the on-screen tag.
- s8: the loop line's opening "So" was dropped.

All fact-check fixes are applied exactly: s2 calorie intake, s3, s4 and s6.

factcheck.summary: I checked every factual claim in this Short against the official labels, and all of them match. s2: Zepbound's prescribing information, section 12.2 (revised 8/2026), says "Tirzepatide decreases calorie intake. The effects are likely mediated by affecting appetite." That sentence isn't limited to type 2 diabetes, so the general wording is correct. Mounjaro's section 12.2 says it "decreases food intake… in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus". s6: Mounjaro section 5.3 says the risk of hypoglycemia "may" be higher with an insulin secretagogue (e.g. a sulfonylurea) or insulin, and Zepbound section 5.7 says hypoglycemia "has also been associated with ZEPBOUND and GLP-1 receptor agonists in adults without type 2 diabetes mellitus". The script and on-screen text keep that scope and hedge. s7 uses the required stomach-pain wording ("severe pain in your stomach area that won't go away, with or without vomiting", "call your healthcare provider right away", "that emergency sign") and the scoped don't-stop line. The label's Medication Guide also says to stop using the drug for this sign; the script leaves that out on purpose, in line with the house line. s5 gives no eating instruction and carries a caveat for anyone with a history of disordered eating, and there's no body-shaming or diet-restriction message anywhere. The Short closes on "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber." as one card ending in a full stop, with no subscribe or link line. I counted 160 spoken words, inside the standard arm. The title and hook are honest, and the Short delivers what they promise. Both sources are the official Lilly labels, and both URLs work. No fixes are needed.
